question: What closes when an ENG BLEED pushbutton is selected OFF?

options.text: The pack flow control valve on that side
The bleed valve and the HP valve, with a white OFF light

explanation: OFF isolates that engine from the pneumatic system completely.

question: Which of these turns on an ENG BLEED FAULT light?

options.text: Overpressure downstream of the bleed valve

explanation: FAULT causes are overpressure, bleed overheat, a wing or engine leak on that side, or the bleed valve failing to close when it must.

question: During an engine start the ENG BLEED FAULT light comes on. Which valve condition causes it?

options.text: The pack flow control valve is open
The bleed valve is not closed during engine start

explanation: The bleed valve must close during start so air goes to the starter; a valve that fails to close gives FAULT.

question: Why would an ENG BLEED FAULT light come on with the APU BLEED pushbutton ON?

options.text: The engine bleed valve has not closed although APU bleed is ON
The cross bleed valve is closed
The APU bleed has a leak

explanation: With APU bleed ON, the engine bleed valves must close so the APU does not feed back into the engines.

question: When does an ENG BLEED FAULT light go out?

options.text: When the pushbutton is selected OFF or the fault has disappeared

explanation: The light reflects the condition; selecting OFF also extinguishes it.

question: With APU BLEED selected ON, when does the APU bleed valve open?

options.text: Immediately, as soon as the APU master switch is ON
Only after both engines have started

explanation: The valve waits until the APU is up to speed; the pushbutton shows a blue ON light.

question: What light does the APU BLEED pushbutton show when selected ON?
explanation: Blue marks a system deliberately selected on that is normally off.

question: What turns on the APU BLEED FAULT light?
explanation: APU BLEED FAULT is a leak detection, with an ECAM caution.

question: With the X BLEED selector in AUTO, when is the cross bleed valve open?

options.text: Whenever one engine bleed is off
When the APU bleed valve is open

explanation: In AUTO the valve follows the APU bleed valve, so the APU can supply both sides.

question: In AUTO, what closes the cross bleed valve even with APU bleed in use (other than during engine start)?

options.text: A wing, pylon or APU leak

explanation: Closing the valve isolates the leaking side from the healthy side.

question: What do the OPEN and CLOSE positions of the X BLEED selector do?

options.text: They select which engine supplies the APU
They open or close the HP valves
They force the cross bleed valve open or closed regardless of the automatic logic

explanation: OPEN and CLOSE are crew overrides of the automatic control.

question: On the BLEED page, when is the precooler inlet pressure shown in amber?
explanation: Too little pressure means the bleed is not supplying; too much indicates a regulation failure.

question: Below what precooler outlet temperature is the indication shown in amber on the BLEED page?
explanation: A low outlet temperature points to a bleed not delivering hot air.

question: The precooler outlet temperature turns amber when it exceeds what value for 5 seconds?
explanation: The high limits are time-based: above 290 °C for 5 s, 270 °C for 15 s or 257 °C for 55 s.

question: When does the high-pressure ground connection symbol appear on the BLEED page?

options.text: Whenever the aircraft is on the ground
When a high-pressure ground air source is connected
When external electrical power is on
When the APU bleed is off

explanation: It is hidden when nothing is connected.

question: When does the anti-ice indication appear on the BLEED page?

options.text: When the probe heat is in AUTO
When the WING anti-ice pushbutton is ON

explanation: The BLEED page shows wing anti-ice because it is a bleed air user.

question: On the ground, when does a user arrow on the BLEED page turn amber?

options.text: As soon as the valve opens
When the engine is at idle
When the corresponding valve has been open for more than 10 seconds

explanation: On the ground wing anti-ice is limited to a short test; a valve left open longer is flagged.

question: When is the engine number shown in amber on the BLEED page?

options.text: When that engine's N2 is below idle
When the engine bleed is off
When the engine is at take-off thrust
When the engine anti-ice is on

explanation: An engine below idle cannot supply bleed air.

question: On the BLEED page, what does an amber crossline on the APU bleed valve mean?

options.text: The cross bleed valve is closed
The APU master and APU BLEED are ON but the valve is closed

explanation: Commanded open but shown closed is a disagreement, so it is amber.

question: When is a crossbleed engine start used?

options.text: When a normal APU bleed start is not possible, usually because the APU is inoperative
When the external power is not available

explanation: Air from the running engine is used to start the second engine.

question: In a crossbleed start, why is the receiving engine's ENG BLEED selected OFF?

options.text: To keep the receiving engine's pack running
To prevent the running engine's air escaping back through the receiving engine
To protect the receiving engine from overheat

explanation: With the bleed valve closed, the air goes to the start valve instead of leaking out through the bleed duct.

question: Where is the X BLEED selector set for a crossbleed engine start?
explanation: The cross bleed valve must be open to join the running engine's duct to the other side.

question: What minimum bleed pressure is required before attempting a start from a crossbleed or an air start unit?
explanation: If the pressure is lower, the running engine's thrust is increased (or the ASU checked) before starting.

question: During a crossbleed start, what pressure should be maintained throughout?
explanation: Pressure often drops as the start valve opens; thrust is added on the supplying engine to keep at least 25 psi.

question: During a crossbleed start, the supplying engine needs about 40 % N1 to keep the pressure. What should the crew consider?

options.text: Selecting the receiving engine bleed ON
Checking the area behind is clear and, if more than 40 % is needed, aborting as the configuration may be wrong

explanation: Needing much power suggests a leak or wrong valve setting, and jet blast becomes a hazard to people behind.

question: After a crossbleed start, what happens to the X BLEED selector?

options.text: It stays OPEN for the flight
It is left in any position

explanation: After both engines run: supplying engine to idle, X BLEED to AUTO, receiving ENG BLEED back ON.

question: When should a crossbleed engine start not be performed?

options.text: During pushback, or where the engine's thrust would endanger people or property

explanation: The supplying engine needs significant thrust, which is dangerous behind the aircraft.

question: Why is external electrical power required for an air start unit (ASU) start?

options.text: Because the inoperative APU is not supplying electrical power
Because the ASU needs electrical power to run
Because the engine starter is electric

explanation: The ASU supplies air only; electrical power has to come from a ground power unit.

question: Before an ASU is connected, how are the packs and the X BLEED selector set?

options.text: Both packs OFF and X BLEED OPEN, with all bleeds OFF
Both packs ON and X BLEED AUTO
Packs ON and X BLEED CLOSE
Packs OFF and X BLEED CLOSE

explanation: All the ASU's air must go to the starter, so nothing else draws on it.
